items.en: What do the boys learn at school?
items.hint: two nouns in the accusative (the objects)

items.en: Who teaches the boys?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject)

items.en: Why can the master teach many things?
items.hint: a reason: he knows ... (with a relative clause)

items.en: What kind of man is the master?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative

items.en: Who is said to be stupid?
items.hint: a relative clause: 'quī ...' (he who ...)
choices: quī in lūdō dormit neque discere vult

items.en: Is any of the boys asleep?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no' (nobody ...)

items.en: Whom does the master tell to sit down last?
items.hint: a name in the accusative (the object)

items.en: Whom does the master question?
items.hint: a name in the accusative (the object)

items.en: How does Titus count?
items.hint: an adverb (how)

items.en: How many numbers is it enough to say?
items.hint: a number with 'numerōs' in the accusative

items.en: Who says 'fifty'?
items.hint: a name in the nominative

items.en: What is Marcus's answer like?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative neuter

items.en: Whom does the master praise?
items.hint: two names in the accusative (the objects)

items.q: Titus et Sextus quālēs discipulī sunt?
items.en: What kind of pupils are Titus and Sextus?
items.hint: two adjectives in the nominative plural

items.en: How many are thirty and seven?
items.hint: a number (cardinal)

items.en: How many are thirty and eight?
items.hint: a number (two from forty)

items.en: How many are thirty and nine?
items.hint: a number (one from forty)

items.q: Cūr magister Mārcum stultum esse dīcit?
items.en: Why does the master say Marcus is stupid?
items.hint: a reason with two adverbs (he answers ...)

items.q: Utrum magister Mārcum laudat an reprehendit?
items.en: Does the master praise Marcus or scold him?
items.hint: a verb, 3rd person singular

items.en: Who are always praised, never scolded?
items.hint: two names in the nominative

items.en: Why is Marcus scolded?
items.hint: a reason with an adverb (he always answers ...)

items.q: Nōnne magister Titum et Sextum saepe interrogat?
items.en: Doesn't the master often question Titus and Sextus?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'nōnne' expects 'yes'

items.q: Cui magister inimīcus est, ut Mārcus dīcit?
items.en: To whom is the master unfriendly, according to Marcus?
items.hint: a noun in the dative (unfriendly to ...)

items.q: Quis saepe laudātur, ut Sextus dīcit?
items.en: Who is often praised, according to Sextus?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject)

items.en: What kind of pupil is Quintus?
items.hint: adjectives in the nominative

items.q: Laetāturne Mārcus cum frāter eius laudātur?
items.en: Is Marcus glad when his brother is praised?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (he is not)

items.q: Cūr Quīntus hodiē laudātur, ut Mārcus dīcit?
items.en: Why is Quintus praised today, according to Marcus?
items.hint: a reason with 'quia' and an infinitive (it is not fitting to ...)

items.en: What does the angry master raise?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object)

items.q: Num puerī magistrum aut virgam eius verentur?
items.en: Surely the boys do not fear the master or his rod?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no'

items.en: From where does the master take out two coins?
items.hint: ablative after 'ex' (out of ...)

items.en: How many asses is one sesterce?
items.hint: a number in the nominative

items.en: How many sesterces are ten denarii?
items.hint: a number (cardinal)

items.en: What kind of answer does Titus give the master?
items.hint: an adjective in the accusative neuter

items.en: How many denarii are forty-eight sesterces?
items.hint: a number with 'dēnāriī' in the nominative

items.en: To whom does Diodorus give an as?
items.hint: a name in the dative (to whom)

items.en: What does the master not give away freely?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object)

items.q: Cūr puerī tot numerōs difficilēs discunt?
items.en: Why do the boys learn so many difficult numbers?
items.hint: a reason with 'quia' and 'necesse est'

items.en: How ought money to be shared?
items.hint: accusative after 'in' (into ... parts)
